The UNO R3 uses a 16 MHz ceramic resonator for the ATmega328P and an ATmega16U2 USB-to-serial bridge. UART0 remains shared with the D0/D1 headers. Board pin constraints, build/flash profiles, and physical-revision confirmation remain open.
The Mega 2560 Rev3 runs the ATmega2560 at 16 MHz and uses an ATmega16U2 USB-to-serial bridge on Serial0. Board pin constraints, build/flash profiles, and physical-revision confirmation remain open.

The Leonardo uses a 16 MHz crystal and the ATmega32U4 native USB controller; it has no secondary USB bridge MCU. USB and UART pin-use constraints, build/flash profiles, and physical-revision confirmation remain open.

The A000005 Nano uses the ATmega328P-32MUR at 16 MHz and an FT232RL USB-to-UART bridge. Keep the profile scoped to this exact SKU; board pin constraints, build/flash settings, and physical-revision confirmation remain open.

The ATmega4809 is specified to run up to 20 MHz. The ATSAMD11D14A is the USB bridge and controls UPDI programming; PB04, PB05, and PA14 are occupied by these connections. The board documentation does not identify a single external main-clock source, so clock_sources stays empty. Build/flash profiles remain open.

This profile is specifically for ESP-WROOM-32 with 4 MiB module flash and a 40 MHz module crystal. DevKitC V4 supports multiple module variants and USB-UART bridge revisions; confirm the fitted parts. GPIO6–GPIO11 are dedicated to module SPI flash. Other pin, build, and flash details remain open.

The board contains an on-board J-Link interface and an nRF52840 board controller. DK v0.14.0 and later adds 8 MiB external SPI flash, which is revision- and routing-dependent and is not the nRF9160 application flash. Clock configuration, exact fitted SiP revision, build profile, and flash profile remain open.

For the MB1367 NUCLEO-G474RE, UM2505 documents the 24 MHz X3 HSE crystal as the default source and an 8 MHz ST-LINK MCO as an alternative. Solder-bridge configuration must be recorded for a physical board before generation. Pin reservations and build/flash profiles remain open.

For MB1137 NUCLEO-F746ZG, the default HSE is the fixed 8 MHz ST-LINK MCO; the 8 MHz X3 crystal is not provided. The 32.768 kHz X2 LSE is the documented default. ST lists the board as out of production. Exact board revision, solder-bridge state, pin reservations, and build/flash profiles remain open.

NUCLEO-H743ZI2 is the MB1364 variant with STLINK-V3E. UM2407 gives an 8 MHz ST-LINK MCO as default HSE, a 25 MHz X3 crystal option (crystal not provided), and a 32.768 kHz X2 LSE default. ST-LINK firmware can change the MCO frequency. Board revision, solder bridges, pin reservations, and build/flash profiles remain open.

The MB1363 H745 board uses 8 MHz ST-LINK MCO as default HSE; UM2408 also documents a 25 MHz X2 HSE crystal path and a default 32.768 kHz X3 LSE crystal. HSE can be changed by solder-bridge configuration and ST-LINK firmware. Board revision, dual-core startup, pin reservations, and build/flash profiles remain open; ST lists this SKU out of production.

UM2488 specifies X1 as a 25 MHz oscillator for the STM32H745XIH6 and Ethernet PHY, X2 as a 32.768 kHz RTC crystal, and X3 as a 25 MHz oscillator for ST-LINK. Confirm board revision and clock configuration before using these values. Dual-core startup, pin reservations, build, and flash profiles remain open.

The MB1363 H755 board uses 8 MHz ST-LINK MCO as default HSE; UM2408 also documents a 25 MHz X2 HSE crystal path and a default 32.768 kHz X3 LSE crystal. HSE can be changed by solder-bridge configuration and ST-LINK firmware. Board revision, dual-core startup, pin reservations, build, and flash profiles remain open.

Selection placeholder only. No physical STM32F722RET6 carrier model, revision, schematic, clock sources, or programming interface has been supplied. Replace this record with the actual board before treating it as a target.

The original non-W Pico provides 2 MiB QSPI flash at the RP2040 XIP base 0x10000000 and a 12 MHz crystal. GPIO23, GPIO24, GPIO25, and GPIO29 are used by on-board SMPS, USB sensing, LED, and VSYS measurement. The XIP linker layout, board revision, build profile, and SWD/USB flash profile remain open.

The non-wireless Pico 2 has 4 MiB QSPI flash mapped through RP2350 XIP at 0x10000000 and a 12 MHz crystal. GPIO23, GPIO24, GPIO25, and GPIO29 are used by the on-board SMPS, USB sensing, user LED, and VSYS measurement. Architecture selection, boot security, linker layout, board revision, and USB/SWD flash profiles remain open.
